main_body: Grey steel safe body, about 16x22 px, with an inset door panel, a yellow dial and a handle on the right
top_band: light grey-blue at rows ~10-12 (about 3 rows), then a near-white edge line at row 13, then the front face
evidence: The column reads as a light grey band at rows 10-12 and a white line at row 13. Everything below, rows 14-30, is the door seen face-on with a dark frame, dial and handle. The top is only about 3 rows against a 22-row object, so it reads as a cap or rim on a front elevation rather than a horizontal surface. There is no clear eave shadow under the edge line. The inset door frame does not make up for the thin top. Under the strict rule this is a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The grey ramp has only about 4 steps: light top, highlight line, mid body, and dark frame. The outline is a uniform near-black, slightly blue-neutral line around the whole shape, which gives the sticker look. The body, door and panel interior are large flat fills with no grain, speckle or per-surface highlights. Most tiles hold only 2-4 colours, well below the stall and well references, which carry tile texture, wood grain and shaded stones.
